selectedWork.title: Adaptive Study Game
selectedWork.label: Interactive learning
selectedWork.description: Choose a topic. Play a round. Find out what sticks.

notes.heading: A study tool I needed myself.
notes.subtitle: Built while I was struggling to study for my final-year paper.
notes.brief: Turn my source material into questions I could play through, explain what I got wrong, and let me practise the questions I missed.
story: I built Adaptive Study Game because reading for my final-year paper was becoming a struggle. I wanted to work through the material as a game, with questions that helped me find out what I actually understood.

An early version became something I played with friends. We sat in a circle, brought our source materials and challenged each other on the questions. But I found it most useful on my own: answer a question, ask why I missed it, review my mistakes and try those questions again.
The sample here is a fixed quiz, separate from the full application. The full app is currently unavailable.

notes.heading: Built for my mother's school.
notes.subtitle: What began with results grew into a shared platform for the school community.
notes.brief: Make preparing results easier, then bring school administration, payments and teaching support into one affordable platform.
story: Melo started because my mother's school needed software, and the existing options were too expensive. I had been building school workflows in Excel, so I began with a problem I already knew: making results easier to prepare.

As I built it, I spoke with schools about the problems they faced. The goal grew into a shared platform for administrators, teachers, parents and students, with access to results, payments and the school's financial picture. I also wanted teachers to have AI-assisted tools for preparing lesson notes and previews.

story: I hadn't made a hyper-edited video since January. When Sharon's birthday came around in December, it felt like the right reason to return to it. She was my manager at the time and is now the COO of the company.

selectedWork.title: Brushes of GOLD
selectedWork.label: Cinematic vlog
selectedWork.description: A Sunday vlog at Elizade University, shot in HDR10+ and graded in DaVinci Resolve.

notes.heading: Could an ordinary Sunday look cinematic?
notes.subtitle: A Sunday vlog at Elizade University, shot in HDR10+ and graded in DaVinci Resolve.
notes.brief: Film a full day and use colour grading to see how cinematic everyday moments could look.
story: I wanted to find out whether I could make an ordinary day look cinematic. I was learning colour grading in DaVinci Resolve, so I decided to film a full Sunday in HDR10+ and grade it afterwards.

At Elizade University, where I was studying, I filmed the campus, went to church and caught up with friends. People smiled, laughed and sometimes ran from the camera. I gave the footage a teal-and-orange look, and the day became a fun way to put what I was learning into practice.
